faq.q: What is included in a Marbella sunset cruise champagne tapas package?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and 21% Spanish VAT. Champagne and tapas are served on board as part of the package.

faq.q: Which boats are available for sunset cruises?
faq.a: Our Tier A boats – Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) – are the most popular for sunset cruises at €749 for 2 hours. Larger yachts like the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) are also available; pricing on request via WhatsApp.

faq.q: What time does a sunset cruise typically depart?
faq.a: In summer (June–August), sunset is around 21:30–21:45, so we recommend departing between 19:00 and 20:00 to enjoy the golden hour and the actual sunset at sea. In spring and autumn, sunset is earlier, and departure times adjust accordingly.

faq.q: Can we bring our own food or drinks?
faq.a: No need – our package already includes champagne, cava, beer, soft drinks, and light tapas. If you have specific dietary requirements, let us know in advance, and we can arrange alternatives. Outside food and drink are not permitted for safety and licensing reasons.

faq.q: How many people can join a sunset cruise?
faq.a: The Astondoa 40 takes up to 9 passengers, and the Azimut 39 takes up to 11. For larger groups (up to 12), we can accommodate on a Mangusta 80 or Azimut 58 Flybridge – pricing on request. All capacities are strictly enforced for safety and comfort.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
faq.a: Your safety is our priority. If the captain deems conditions unsafe (e.g. high winds or storms), we will reschedule or offer a full refund. We monitor forecasts closely and will contact you 24–48 hours before departure if any issues arise.

faq.q: Do we need to tip the skipper?
faq.a: Tipping is not mandatory, but it is appreciated. If you enjoyed the experience, a 10% tip for the skipper is customary in Marbella. All gratuities go directly to the crew.

faq.q: How do I book a sunset cruise?
faq.a: You can book directly on our website or send us a WhatsApp message. For Tier A boats, select your date and pay online. For larger yachts, we will confirm availability and pricing within 2 hours. A 50% deposit secures the booking; balance is due 48h before departure.

data.body_html:
There is no better way to end a day on the Costa del Sol than with a Marbella sunset cruise champagne tapas 2037 experience. As the sun sinks behind La Concha and the Mediterranean turns to gold, you will sip chilled champagne, nibble on Spanish tapas, and glide past the superyachts of Puerto Banús. Our fleet includes the Astondoa 40 (€749 for 2 hours) and the Azimut 39, both fully equipped with a licensed skipper, drinks, snacks, and all taxes. Whether you are celebrating an anniversary, a birthday, or simply the beauty of the evening, this is Marbella at its most magical.

Why choose a sunset cruise in Marbella?

Marbella’s coastline offers some of the best sunset views in Europe. From the water, you see the Sierra Blanca mountains, the Golden Mile, and the glittering marina of Puerto Banús in a different light. A sunset cruise lets you escape the crowded beach clubs and enjoy the 25 °C evening air, the gentle swell, and the colours that change every minute. Our Boat Rental Marbella hub has more ideas for sea experiences, but nothing beats the combination of champagne, tapas, and a setting sun.

What’s included in the champagne & tapas package?

Every sunset charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light tapas (olives, Iberian ham, cheese, bread, and seasonal bites). Insurance and 21% Spanish VAT are also covered. You do not need to bring anything except your sunglasses and a camera. The champagne is served upon departure, and the tapas are laid out as you anchor near Cabopino or Cala del Faro.

For larger groups or a more luxurious experience, the Mangusta 80 (from €4,719 for 4 hours, includes a free jet ski) or the Azimut 58 Flybridge are excellent choices. Book your sunset cruise directly online or via WhatsApp for a custom quote.

Best time for a sunset cruise in 2037

Sunset times in Marbella vary by month. In July 2037, sunset is around 21:42; in September, around 20:35. We recommend departing 1.5 to 2 hours before official sunset so you can cruise out, anchor for a swim (if conditions allow), and watch the sun dip below the horizon. Our team will confirm the exact departure time when you book.

What to expect on board

Your skipper will welcome you at Puerto Banús (next to the Casino). After a quick safety briefing, you will motor out past the famous port, heading west towards Estepona or east towards Cabopino. The boat has a shaded saloon, a sun deck, and a sound system – you can connect your own playlist. The champagne will be poured, and the tapas will be served as you relax. Most sunset cruises last 2 hours, but you can extend to 3 or 4 hours for a longer dinner on the water (pricing on request).

How to book your sunset cruise

Booking is simple. Choose your preferred boat and date on our website, pay a 50% deposit, and we will send you a confirmation. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), the price is fixed at €749 for 2 hours. For larger yachts, send us a WhatsApp message with your group size and preferred date, and we will reply within 2 hours with availability and a custom quote. Balance payment is due 48 hours before departure. Cancellations made more than 48 hours in advance are fully refundable.
